login_failed.title: HA Xplora® Watch could not sign in
login_failed.description:
Home Assistant could not sign in to the Xplora® account **{account}** ({error}).

This usually means the password changed, the account was moved, or the address no longer exists. Open **Settings → Devices & Services → HA Xplora® Watch** and use **Reconfigure** on that account to enter the new sign-in details — you do not have to delete and re-add the integration, so your entities, their recorded history and the stored location archive are kept.

init.description: Everything on this page is optional. Polling is off by default, so Home Assistant only contacts Xplora® when you ask it to.
init.title: HA Xplora® Watch settings

data_description.account_alias: Renames this account's watch device (e.g. “Dana Watch (Mom)”) on the next reload. Existing entity ids keep their original name, so automations and dashboards that reference them keep working.
data_description.watches: Which of this account's watches Home Assistant creates a device and entities for. A deselected watch keeps its entities, but they stop updating.

data.refresh_on_card_render: Refresh data when dashboard cards are shown
data.scan_interval_functions: Functions update interval (alarms, silent times, safe zones)

data_description.refresh_on_card_render: When on, the custom dashboard cards request fresh data as soon as they are shown (alarms and silent times, location, and chat). Off by default to minimise API traffic; when several cards in one view show the same watch, each data set is refreshed only once.
data_description.scan_interval: How often Home Assistant polls the watches for battery, location and status. Off (the default) disables automatic polling — updates then come only from the xplora_watch.see service or pressing the Update location button.
data_description.scan_interval_functions: How often the rarely-changing alarms, silent times and safe-zone definitions are fetched. Each needs a separate request per watch, so this is Off by default to minimise traffic. Choose 'With every poll' to refresh them on each update, or fetch them on demand with the xplora_watch.refresh_functions service or by tapping the count tiles on the card.

data_description.home_is_safezone: When on, the “Outside safe zone” sensor also treats Home Assistant's home zone (latitude/longitude/radius below) as a safe zone, on top of the zones configured in the Xplora® app.
data_description.home_latitude: Only used by the “Outside safe zone” sensor when “Home is Safezone” is on. Defaults to your Home Assistant home zone; override it here if the watch's safe zone is a different place.
data_description.home_longitude: Only used by the “Outside safe zone” sensor when “Home is Safezone” is on.
data_description.home_radius: Radius in metres of the home area used by the “Outside safe zone” sensor.
data_description.maps: Which geocoding service turns a position into a street address. “OpenStreetMap” is free and keyless; “OpenCage” needs the API key below and is more precise.
data_description.opencage_apikey: Only needed when Maps is set to OpenCage. Get a free key at opencagedata.com.

data.auto_mark_read: Mark chat messages as read while polling

data_description.auto_mark_read: When on, messages fetched for the chat card are marked as read on the watch. Leave off if the child should still see them as unread on the watch itself.
data_description.message: How many recent chat messages are kept per watch. Larger values mean more history in the chat card and a bigger attribute on the Unread messages sensor.
data_description.remove_message: When on, messages deleted in the Xplora® app are still shown in the chat card.

data_description.notify_call: Fire a Home Assistant event, and write a logbook line, for each call (incoming, outgoing, missed). Off by default. Only fires while polling is on. The logbook line records the contact's phone number and name into the Home Assistant recorder database — a deliberate trade for visibility, not a privacy guarantee. Leave off if you do not want contact numbers stored in your database.
data_description.notify_low_power: Fire a Home Assistant event, and write a logbook line, when the watch reports low battery. Off by default. Only fires while polling is on.
data_description.notify_power: Fire a Home Assistant event, and write a logbook line, when the watch powers on or off. Off by default. Only fires while polling is on.
data_description.notify_sos: Fire a Home Assistant event, and write a logbook line, when the watch sends an SOS. On by default. Only fires while polling is on. The logbook line records the SOS location (latitude/longitude) into the Home Assistant recorder database — a deliberate trade for visibility, not a privacy guarantee.

data_description.auto_fetch_history: When on, the integration fetches the previous day's location track at 01:00 local time — only if that day's data is not already cached. Useful if you want a growing location archive without setting up your own automation calling xplora_watch.fetch_history daily.
data_description.history_retention_days: How long the location-history sensor keeps past positions. Home Assistant retains far more than the Xplora® app's ~3-day window.

data_description.signin_typ: Shown for information only — it is how this account signs in. To switch between e-mail and phone sign-in, use Reconfigure on the integration entry.
data_description.language: Language used for this integration's dialogs, its services' day names, and the log messages it writes.
